speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance and location of your skin lesions, and tell me exactly where you are feeling pain in your wrist?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the pattern of migrating joint pain, did you notice a red, expanding "bullseye" rash or a tick bite on your skin during or after the trip? Also, are you experiencing any headache, fatigue, or neck stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists and hands is highly specific and concerning for secondary syphilis. Have you noticed any painless sores (chancres) on your genitals or in your mouth in the recent past?

REQUEST TEST: RPR

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative RPR result makes secondary syphilis unlikely, despite the suspicious lesions. Given the monoarticular swelling, severe tenderness, fever, and history of prior knee pain, I need to rule out septic arthritis or Lyme disease.
